trends.note: 2021 dip reflects COVID-19 reporting gaps; 2023 shows pandemic rebound.

riskFactors.title: HIV Co-Infection
riskFactors.description: People living with HIV are 18x more likely to develop active TB disease. HIV/TB co-infection accounted for 167,000 deaths in 2023.

riskFactors.title: Drug-Resistant TB (MDR-TB)
riskFactors.description: MDR-TB requires 18–24 months of treatment with toxic drugs. Treatment success rate is only 57% vs 88% for drug-susceptible TB.

riskFactors.title: Poverty & Malnutrition
riskFactors.description: Malnutrition accounts for 19% of global TB incidence. Overcrowding and poor ventilation significantly accelerate transmission.

riskFactors.title: Tobacco Smoking
riskFactors.description: Smokers are 2.5x more likely to develop active TB and experience worse treatment outcomes.

riskFactors.title: Diabetes Mellitus
riskFactors.description: Diabetics are 3x more likely to develop active TB. Diabetes accounts for approximately 15% of TB cases in high-burden countries.

didYouKnow: One quarter of the world's population has latent TB infection — the bacteria is present but not yet causing disease.
TB kills more people than any other single infectious agent globally, except COVID-19.
India alone accounts for 27% of all new TB cases worldwide.
Drug-resistant TB costs up to 100x more to treat than drug-susceptible TB.

faq.q: Is tuberculosis still a global threat in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. TB remains the world's deadliest infectious disease (excluding COVID-19), killing 1.25 million people annually. The COVID-19 pandemic reversed years of hard-won progress by disrupting health services.

MDR-TB is caused by bacteria resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin — the two most powerful first-line anti-TB drugs. It requires longer, more expensive treatment regimens with significantly lower success rates.
Yes. Drug-susceptible TB is curable in 6 months with a standard 4-drug regimen. Global treatment success stands at 88%. MDR-TB is also treatable but requires 18-24 months of therapy.
